subject: Post-call: Deployment mode & compliance next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: John Smith <john.smith@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Deployment mode & compliance next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi John —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the follow-ups we agreed on: 

Call highlights:
- Primary workload: PHI processing for patient intake and triage (low concurrency, moderate RPS spikes during business hours).
- Primary compliance needs: HIPAA + BAA required, SOC2 evidence requested by internal audit.
- Preference: minimize engineering lift but must meet audit/BAA controls.

Deployment options we discussed (quick pros/cons):
- Hosted API: fastest to go-live; Redwood manages runtime and SOC2 controls; can sign BAA; shared tenancy so may not meet some procurement controls around dedicated isolation.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs): predictable throughput, tenant isolation at infra layer, can be contracted with SLA and stricter access controls; good middle ground.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full network isolation and customer-managed infra; required for some regulated workflows or when customer needs on-prem auditability — higher operational effort and longer lead time.

Next steps (agreed):
1) I will send the SOC2 summary and a draft BAA for your security team to review (attached).
2) Marissa (post-sales) to share pricing/commit template for Dedicated vs Hosted and expected lead times.
3) John to confirm any mandatory on-prem/hard isolation requirements from procurement by EOD Thursday.

Questions for you before we loop in procurement:
- Any mandatory controls beyond HIPAA/BAA + SOC2 (e.g., specific KMS/HSM requirements, data residency restrictions)?
- Do you have a preferred model for isolation (Dedicated vs VPC vs on-prem)?

Attaching: Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf (excerpt), Redwood_BAA_draft.docx (BAA draft).

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick call if helpful.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the recap and the attachments — received both. Quick answers from my side: 

- Procurement is primarily asking for two things: 1) SOC2 Type II report or an attestation summary (we understand you shared an excerpt; procurement may ask for a last 12-month coverage date), and 2) a signed BAA.
- For isolation, they prefer Dedicated capacity as a first option (we still want Redwood to manage the infra) but if you require it, we can evaluate VPC/private if procurement flags any issues. Important: we cannot go fully on-prem at this stage.
- KMS: we do require customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for production PHI workloads.

Can you confirm whether Dedicated + BYOK is supported and what the expected timeline to provision Dedicated would be? Also, any additional evidence your security team can provide for procurement (subprocessor list, encryption at rest/in-transit details) would be helpful.

Thanks — John

Thanks John — great context. Answers inline and next steps below.

- SOC2: The attached Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf includes last Type II coverage dates and our compliance owner contact. If procurement needs the full report, we typically provide an encrypted report under NDA; we can start that process.
- BAA: we can sign a BAA. I attached a draft (Redwood_BAA_draft.docx) for your legal to review.
- Dedicated + BYOK: Supported. We offer customer-managed KMS for Dedicated deployments (AWS KMS, Cloud HSM integration). For Hosted API we also offer BYOK in some tiers but Dedicated is the simplest path to guarantee separation and control.
- Timeline: Dedicated provisioning (reserved capacity) typically takes 2–4 weeks from contract signature and KMS provisioning; VPC/private can take 4–8+ weeks depending on network reviews and any on-prem requirements.
- Evidence: will share subprocessors list, encryption-in-transit at TLS1.2+/mTLS, key management docs, and our SOC2 resource. Marissa will send the procurement packet with pricing and contract term comparisons (Hosted vs Dedicated) by EOD today.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Marissa to share pricing/commit options + procurement packet (today).
2) John to confirm critical must-haves (BYOK yes/no, any data residency) so we can mark Dedicated as the preferred path.
3) I will introduce our security contact and start the encrypted SOC2 report request if procurement needs the full artifact.
4) If procurement agrees to Dedicated, Marissa will kick off SOW and expected provisioning timeline.

Attaching: Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf (again), Redwood_BAA_draft.docx.

Happy to set up a 30-min procurement sync if helpful.

Best,
Rishi
